question.text: Why is NISM certification required for approved users, sales personnel, and dealers of trading members handling derivative transactions?

answer.text: To ensure a minimum common knowledge benchmark on derivative products, risks, trading, clearing, settlement, and the regulatory framework for approved users, sales personnel, and dealers of trading members
NISM certification is optional and only provides a competitive advantage; it is not a regulatory requirement
NISM certification is required only for equity derivative dealers, not for currency or interest rate derivative dealers
NISM certification is a one-time qualification with no renewal requirement and covers all financial products

explanation.text: The Logic: NISM certification is mandated as a minimum common knowledge benchmark for approved users, sales personnel, and dealers of trading members in the derivatives segments. It tests knowledge of products, risks, trading, clearing, settlement, and the applicable regulatory framework. The Trap: The requirement is not optional, is not confined to equity derivatives, and is segment-specific rather than a single lifetime qualification covering all financial products. Note: Different NISM series cover different derivative segments; the benchmark applies to the relevant approved users, sales personnel, and dealers of the trading member, not to every market role.
